goal: commerce.pages has three stored generated columns (published_title, published_titles, remembered_modal) that the database fills for every writer, and publishedPageNames(), usesRememberedModals() and the page index read them instead of digging through page documents.
why: Today menus pull titles out of each page's JSON (57,930 calls in 78 days) and the consent banner runs jsonb_path_exists over every published page of a site for one yes or no (68,878 calls, 121 s). Content, one statement: create or replace function commerce.page_titles(p jsonb) returns jsonb language sql immutable set search_path to '' as $$ select coalesce(jsonb_object_agg(t.key, t.value ->> 'title') filter (where coalesce(t.value ->> 'title', '') <> ''), '{}'::jsonb) from jsonb_each(case when jsonb_typeof(p -> 'translations') = 'object' then p -> 'translations' else '{}'::jsonb end) t $$; A null p gives '{}'. The function must be immutable (a generated column refuses anything else) and must keep 'set search_path' (src/db/vat.test.ts holds a fixed search_path on every function). This file must sort BEFORE the generated file of the next change: make it first.

((@.frequency == "session" || @.frequency == "days" || !exists(@.frequency)) && (@.triggers.exitIntent == true || exists(@.triggers.timer)))'), false)`). Do not hand-edit the generated file except to confirm its timestamp sorts after page_titles_fn.

Add cases (the file applies every migration to PGlite; follow its nearest pages case for how a store and a page row are made): (1) insert a page naming its columns as savePage() does (store_id, type, slug, draft, published, published_at) with published = {title:'About', translations:{'nb-NO':{title:'Om oss'},'sv-SE':{}}, rows:[]}: published_title is 'About', published_titles is {"nb-NO":"Om oss"}, remembered_modal is false. (3) update only draft: the three columns do not change. (4) set published = null (an unpublish): published_title is null, published_titles is '{}', remembered_modal is false. (5) an insert that tries to write published_title fails (the error names a generated column). (6) the rule in SQL and in code agree: import remembersClose from src/lib/page-modal.ts (it exists today: frequency is not 'always' and a timer or exit intent opens the modal by itself; it does not need step 2.14). Write these five samples as a const in the test, each with key 'm' and size 'md', and for each set published = {rows:[{modal: sample}]} on one page and expect remembered_modal to equal both remembersClose(sample) and the boolean written beside it: {triggers:{timer:{seconds:5},button:true}, frequency:'session'} true; {triggers:{button:true}, frequency:'session'} false; {triggers:{exitIntent:true}, frequency:'days', days:7} true; {triggers:{timer:{seconds:5}}, frequency:'always'} false; {triggers:{className:'open-promo'}, frequency:'days', days:7} false.

migration.notes: Two files in the first commit. (1) Custom: commerce.page_titles(jsonb), an immutable SQL function with a fixed search_path (pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name page_titles_fn, then node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs). (2) Generated by pnpm db:generate from src/db/schema.ts: alter table commerce.pages add three stored generated columns. Add only: no rename, no drop, no backfill, no writer changes, so the code that is running keeps working while the deploy finishes (every insert into pages names its columns; the tests of the copy paths prove it). commerce.pages is not on the hot-table list, so no concurrent file is needed; adding a stored generated column rewrites the table under a lock, which is instant at about 1,400 rows and fits the 15 s statement limit and 5 s lock wait. No index is added. CI's release job applies both files after the checks pass; never apply them by hand. The readers (second commit) may ride in the same push: the release job applies the files before the deploy. They must never be pushed BEFORE the migration commit. After the deploy check the security and performance advisors of project ybsozesfuxuitoacntfo and record the versions.
